issues.legal_issue: The practice of a profession is included within “business” for the purpose of a landlord seeking possession of non-residential premises to carry on that profession.
material_facts: The landlord, an advocate, sought eviction of a tenant from non-residential premises so that he could practise his profession there.
The final court of fact found that the landlord bona fide required the premises for that purpose and that the tenancy could not be split.
The tenant was using the premises to manufacture art jewellery.
The governing rent-control legislation used the term “business” in its ground for eviction concerning non-residential premises and did not separately refer to professions.
issues.conclusion: The practice of law is “business” within the meaning of the statutory eviction ground, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 10(3)(a)(iii) of the Andhra Pradesh Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1960, “business” takes its meaning from the context of that Act and is broad enough to include the practice of a profession. Reading it narrowly would unjustifiably exclude members of the liberal professions from the eviction ground. The Court distinguished M.P. Sethurama Menon v. Meenakshi Amma, Bangalore Water-Supply & Sewerage Board v. R. Rajappa, and Stuchbery v. General Accident Fire and Life Assurance Corporation Ltd. because their statutory contexts differed; it noted Re Williams’ Will Trusts and Taramal v. Laxman Sewak Surey as decisions supporting a broad contextual meaning.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_case and nonresidential_premises and landlord_seeks_premises_for_professional_practice and bona_fide_requirement_found

predicates.rent_control_eviction_case: The proceeding concerns a landlord's claim to recover premises under rent-control law.
predicates.landlord_seeks_premises_for_professional: The landlord seeks the premises to carry on a profession there.
predicates.bona_fide_requirement_found: The fact-finding court found that the landlord genuinely required the premises for the stated purpose.
predicates.professional_practice_qualifies_as_busin: The landlord's professional practice falls within the meaning of business for the eviction ground.

issues.definition: When a landlord in a rent-control eviction proceeding genuinely seeks non-residential premises to practise a profession there, that professional practice qualifies as business for the eviction ground.
